subject: Urgent: Checkout latency surge & fragmented headers from client SDK causing 5xxs (QuickRetail)
messages:
From: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@quickretail.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Cc: dana.liu@checkoutly.io
Date: 2029-03-31T15:20:00Z
Subject: Sudden p99 latency & 500s on /v1/checkouts - started 3/31 11:10AM PT

Hi Karthik / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sharp spike in checkout latency and a rising 500 error rate on our live site starting ~11:10AM PT. Affects ~12% of requests to /v1/checkouts; p95 from 220ms -> 1.8s, p99 > 6s. Traffic hasn't changed on our side. Attaching a short log extract and a PCAP of a sample session.

Two notes from our SRE runbook:
- The errors correlate with clients using SDK v2.3.1 (we've rolled back a small cohort to v2.2.8 and errors drop immediately).
- We see header reassembly warnings in our proxy logs (truncated headers / duplicate X-Request-Id).

Can you confirm if there were infra changes? This is impacting checkout throughput; CS is getting tickets. We need an ETA and mitigation.

Attachments: quickretail_sdk_logs.txt, pcap_sample.zip

—Sam
Sam Ortega
SRE Lead, QuickRetail

"header_reassembly_warning: fragment_count=3; header_truncated=true; x-request-id=..."

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2029-03-31T16:18:00Z
Subject: EXEC ESCALATION: QuickRetail live checkout degradation — suspected client SDK header fragmentation bug

Team — moving to internal thread. QuickRetail is experiencing significant p99 latency and 5xxs on /v1/checkouts; their telemetry strongly correlates failures with our client SDK v2.3.1. They observed parser-level header-split errors and proxy-side header reassembly warnings.

Priority asks:
- Rishi: please confirm whether server-side runtime observed any unusual header fragments, KV cache invalidations, or backpressure-induced frame coalescing during the 11:00–12:00PT window.
- Lauren: we need a short rollback / mitigation plan (pin clients to v2.2.8, temporary rate-limit or route to compatible model variant) and an estimate for a patch if SDK is implicated.
- Monica: please coordinate with QuickRetail CS on immediate customer messaging and interim credits if SLA breach confirmed.

I am copying Marissa for executive visibility — we'll need a short exec briefing (1 slide) if this becomes a longer outage.

I'll attach server traces in the next update.

—Karthik
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2029-04-01T02:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EXEC ESCALATION: QuickRetail live checkout degradation — suspected client SDK header fragmentation bug

Investigated the 11:00–12:00PT window against runtime traces and ingress logs. Findings so far:

- We see a statistically significant increase in fragmented header frames arriving from front-proxies associated with QuickRetail sessions. Upstream packets show split pseudo-headers (Content-Length / Transfer-Encoding) arriving across multiple frames and our parser enters a slow-path that defers header reassembly.
- The slow-path includes an O(N) reassembly in the presence of many small fragments which spikes CPU on the ingress thread; during peaks the KV cache saw thrash and tokenization latency increased leading to p99 amplification.
- Correlated client agent strings: requests with "redwood-sdk/2.3.1" have 3.7x higher probability of inducing the header-split pattern than v2.2.8.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered):
1) Advise QuickRetail to pin the checkout fleet to redwood-sdk v2.2.8 (fast rollback) — stopgap that empirically reduces errors.
2) At ingress layer, enable a short-lived relaxed header coalescing policy for QuickRetail routes to accept split pseudo-headers and coalesce them in the L7 proxy (config change, low-risk).
3) Ship a hotfix to the SDK parser that avoids the pathological reassembly slow-path (ETA: 48–72 hours with high-priority patching).

I filed INF-8721 and attached traces in the ticket. I'm available to pair with QuickRetail SRE for a guided rollback.

—Rishi
Principal SWE, Runtime
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: EXEC ESCALATION: QuickRetail live checkout degradation — suspected client SDK header fragmentation bug

Thanks for the quick triage and clear mitigation plan. Actions we need immediately:

- Karthik & Lauren: coordinate the rollback playbook with QuickRetail ops (they want a hands-on rollback). Provide step-by-step and a runbook for pinning to v2.2.8.
- Rishi: please prioritize the INF-8721 hotfix as P0 and prepare a short risk/rollback note for the release. Add testcases that simulate fragmented pseudo-headers.
- Exec brief: Karthik — can you produce a single-slide incident summary (impact, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, ETA for fix) for EOD? I'll share with VP of Sales + COO.

Also: once stabilized we should run a quick customer post-mortem and review SDK release gating for parser-related changes.

I'll join the coordination call at +1 if needed.

—Marissa
